summary: Pursued the open safety direction with a successor execution: the harness now adds a voter_promoted_after_snapshot case (demote the non-leader peer, snapshot, promote it again so the committed configuration has two voters while the node's snapshot metadata records one) and, after the bounded leadership wait, stops the other instance and attempts one commit with a 1000 ms Apply timeout; it also reconnects the restarted instance's transport with any instance still running. Local feedback before submission: with the flag enabled the restarted voter held latest_config_voters 1 against the 2 in its own log, became Leader with zero election requests, and completed the commit with the other member stopped; with the flag disabled it held the committed two-voter configuration and could neither win leadership nor commit. Eight comparisons are declared (new-shape voter count with its control, election support sought or not, commit completes or not, plus the two established divergence predicates as in-run controls); validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Not yet done: no interpretation was added this turn, and the earlier harness gap (events were emitted correctly, but the peer-stop step needed the reconnection fix) was found only through local verification, so the formal result of this experiment is still outstanding.
